places.title: Quattro Canti
places.description: The beating heart of Palermo, Quattro Canti square is a magnificent example of Sicilian Baroque. Here the four main streets of the city intersect, surrounded by splendid decorated facades.
places.fullDescription: Also known as Piazza Vigliena and called the Teatro del Sole, Quattro Canti is a surprising monumental crossroads designed between 1608 and 1620. The four concave facades that define the square are decorated with fountains, allegories of the seasons, statues of Spanish sovereigns and the patron saints of the historic districts. The overall composition transforms the intersection into a theatrical octagon: it is the ideal starting point to visit the historic center of Palermo.

places.title: San Giovanni degli Eremiti
places.description: A jewel of Norman architecture, famous for its red domes and the peaceful atmosphere of its gardens. An ideal place to immerse yourself in Palermo's millenary history.
places.fullDescription: San Giovanni degli Eremiti, dating back to the 12th century, is an emblematic example of the encounter between Norman art and Arab influences. The distinctive red domes, the cloister with twin columns and the quiet inner garden offer a collected atmosphere that contrasts with the energy of the city center. The complex, near the Palazzo dei Normanni, tells the complex cultural history of Palermo in the Middle Ages.

places.title: Piazza Pretoria
places.description: Famous for its imposing monumental fountain, Piazza Pretoria is a symbol of the city. The marble statues and surrounding architecture create a suggestive and romantic atmosphere.
places.fullDescription: Piazza Pretoria is dominated by the monumental Pretoria Fountain, a Renaissance masterpiece originally from Florence and transferred to Palermo at the end of the 16th century. The fountain is rich in statues of deities, nymphs and allegorical figures — which is why it was nicknamed the Fountain of Shame. Around it stand the Palazzo Pretorio, the church of Santa Caterina and other historic palaces.

places.title: Palermo Cathedral
places.description: An imposing building that blends Arab, Norman and Gothic styles. The Cathedral dominates Palermo's skyline with its towers and millenary history.
places.fullDescription: Palermo Cathedral, founded in the 12th century and modified over different eras, is a true stone book about the history of the island: Arab-Norman, Gothic, Baroque and Neoclassical elements coexist in its structures. Inside, royal tombs and a rich liturgical treasury are preserved. Climbing to the terraces offers a striking view over the historic center.

places.title: Palatine Chapel and Palazzo dei Normanni
places.description: The oldest royal palace in Europe, famous for its extraordinary Byzantine mosaics. The Palatine Chapel is a masterpiece of Arab-Norman art with breathtaking decorations.
places.fullDescription: The Royal Imperial Palatine Chapel is a Siculo-Norman basilica, consecrated in 1140 by King Roger II of Sicily. Located inside the Palazzo dei Normanni, the chapel combines Norman, Arab and Byzantine elements with golden mosaics and a muqarnas wooden ceiling. Since 2015 it has been a UNESCO World Heritage Site and the oldest royal residence in Europe.

places.title: Teatro Massimo
places.description: One of the largest and most majestic opera houses in Europe. The neoclassical architecture and art nouveau interiors create an atmosphere of great suggestion.
places.fullDescription: Teatro Massimo is one of the largest opera houses in Europe, renowned for its excellent acoustics and over 1,300 seats. It hosts more than 130 musical, opera and dance events every year. The exterior is neoclassical with influences from Sicilian Greek temples, while the interior is art nouveau. Built at the end of the 19th century, it is a symbol of the city and an international cultural landmark.

places.title: Ballarò Market
places.description: A historic market rich in colors, scents and authentic flavors. Perfect for savoring the true essence of Sicilian cuisine and immersing yourself in everyday Palermitan life.
places.fullDescription: The Ballarò Market is one of the oldest and most lively markets in Palermo, a true theater of Sicilian daily life. Through its streets intertwine scents of oriental spices, vivid colors of local fruit and vegetables, and the calls of vendors. It is the perfect place to taste Palermitan street food: arancine, panelle, crocchè and other local specialties. The market represents the multicultural soul of the city.

places.title: Botanical Garden
places.description: A green oasis in the heart of Palermo, ideal for a relaxing break among exotic plants and centuries-old trees.
places.fullDescription: The Palermo Botanical Garden, founded in 1789, is one of the most important in Europe. It extends over about 10 hectares and hosts more than 12,000 plant species from around the world. Walking through its avenues you can admire tropical plants, succulents, monumental trees and historic greenhouses. It is a perfect place to escape city chaos and immerse yourself in peace and natural beauty.

places.title: Church of the Gesù (Casa Professa)
places.description: A masterpiece of Sicilian Baroque with spectacular frescoes, polychrome marbles and inlaid decorations. A must-see for art and history lovers.
places.fullDescription: The Church of the Gesù, also known as Casa Professa, is considered one of the most important examples of Baroque art in Sicily. Built by the Jesuits in the 16th century, it amazes with polychrome marbles, gilded stuccos, frescoes and inlays. The interiors are a triumph of Sicilian Baroque art, where every surface is decorated with artisanal mastery.

object.title: 1. Subject Matter
object.description: These general terms govern the booking and stay at Thalea Apartment, located at Via Cagliari 5, Palermo.

booking.title: 2. Bookings
items: The booking is considered confirmed upon receipt of the email confirmation.
At the time of booking, partial or full payment may be required as a guarantee.
The guest must provide accurate and up-to-date details at the time of booking.

payment.title: 3. Payments
payment.description1: Payments can be made by credit card, debit card or other supported electronic methods (Stripe, PayPal).
payment.description2: The full balance must be paid within the deadline indicated in the booking confirmation.

cancellation.title: 4. Cancellations

Do not exceed the maximum number of guests indicated in the booking.
